title: Rock Bottom
description:
Dawn. {name} stared at the empty account screen.

This time he'd blown even the borrowed money.
A number with no way to repay it sat on the screen.

His body shook. Not from cold.

Catching himself thinking about the next bet — {name} felt a chill.
Even now, he was calculating one hand to win it all back.

This was the bottom.
Nowhere left to fall. The real bottom.

Here there were two roads. Reach out a hand, or dig deeper.

choices.text: Ask for help — call a gambling recovery group
choices.result_text:
With trembling hands, he dialed the recovery group's number.

An unfamiliar voice answered. "Yes, we're here. Take your time."

{name} couldn't speak for a while.
Then, barely, one sentence. "...I want to quit gambling."

A quiet reply came through the phone.
"Well done. That one sentence is the hardest."

Hitting bottom also meant the only way left was up.
At least, {name} chose to believe that.

He called his father. It was 4 AM.

He told him everything. The gambling, the debt, the ruined account, the ruined self.
He cried while talking. The first time since becoming an adult.

Father was silent for a long time.
Then he said, low:
"...Come home. Just come once."

He didn't scold. That hurt more.
The son who paid off his father's debt six years ago was now confessing his own debt to his father.
This had to be a new beginning, not an end.

choices.text: One more hand — win it all back with this
choices.result_text:
{name} didn't ask for help.

'Just one hand. I've got a good feeling this time.'

He scraped together the last of his money and bet it.

The result — I won't bother writing it down.
Below the place he thought was bottom, there was another bottom.

Addiction keeps renewing the floor like that.
{name} was learning this fact the most expensive way possible.

title: The First Week Clean
description:
One week since quitting gambling.

It was far harder than expected.
His hand kept reaching for the phone. He wanted to reinstall the deleted apps.
Nights were the most dangerous. When betting time came, his body reacted first.

So this was withdrawal.
Not just for alcohol or cigarettes.

{name} shoved his hands in his pockets and endured.
A week. Just one week. But that week felt like a year.

choices.text: Endure day by day — circle each day on the calendar
choices.result_text:
{name} bought a calendar.

For each gambling-free day, he drew a circle.
One, two, three… the circles grew.

It seemed like nothing, but those circles were strangely a source of strength.
Quitting wasn't a grand resolution — it was one circle for today.

One more tomorrow. That was enough.

choices.text: Work the body — go running every dawn
choices.result_text:
Whenever he wanted to bet, {name} put on running shoes.

He ran the dawn Han River. Breathless, legs aching.
But that pain was honest. Different from the pain of gambling.

Returning drenched in sweat, the urge to bet faded a little.

Covering addiction with something else wasn't a perfect solution, but —
at least tonight, he didn't turn on the phone.

title: The Temptation, Again
description:
About a month clean.

Just when he thought he was okay, it came.

An old betting buddy got in touch.
"Hyung, I've got a sure thing this time. Just come once with me."

{name}'s heart raced. That feeling came alive again.
'Just once... I can control it now, right.'

The most dangerous words for someone who quit
were 'I can control it now.'

His finger froze over the reply.

choices.text: Refuse — 'Sorry, I don't do that anymore'
choices.result_text:
{name} sent the reply.

'Sorry. I don't do that anymore. You should ease up too.'

After sending, he stared at the phone a while.
His heart still raced, but this time — he won.

Quitting wasn't one resolution, but a choice every time.
Today, {name} won that choice.

Win once, and the next time gets a little easier.
Believing that, he set the phone down.

'Just once.'

{name} went.
And it wasn't just once.

A month of circles, erased in one night.
The week of withdrawal, the dawn runs — all of it became nothing.

Addiction waits. For the moment the one who quit lets his guard down and thinks 'I'm fine now.'

{name} had to start again from the collapsed place.
This time, with a heavier heart.

title: Thirty Circles
description:
He looked at the calendar.

The circles passed thirty.
Days spent without gambling were crossing from one month to two.

{name} stared at those circles a long time.

The lost money won't come back. That's a fact.
But what he almost lost — himself, family, the rest of his life — that, he reclaimed.

Gambling was the most expensive lesson for {name}.
The tuition hurt, but he graduated.

Now Gangnam had to be reached another way — not by betting.

choices.result_text:
{name} taped the calendar to the front of his desk.

Every day, looking at those circles, he resolved:
Never to return to that bottom again.

Someone who overcame addiction isn't a weak person.
They're the strongest — someone who saw the bottom and climbed back up.

For the time remaining, {name} would go honestly.
Slow, but certain.

The circles would keep growing. One each day.
